subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In the fluid mosaic model, the basic structural framework of the membrane is the:
questions.explain: Phospholipids form a bilayer with hydrophilic heads outward and hydrophobic tails inward; proteins are embedded in this fluid mosaic.

questions.q: Movement of oxygen across a membrane, from high to low concentration without energy or proteins, is:
questions.explain: Small nonpolar molecules diffuse directly through the bilayer down their concentration gradient.

questions.q: Facilitated diffusion differs from active transport because it:
options: Does not require ATP and moves substances down a gradient
questions.explain: Facilitated diffusion is passive, using channel or carrier proteins to move solutes down their gradient.

questions.q: A red blood cell placed in pure (distilled) water will:
options: Swell and may burst as water enters by osmosis
questions.explain: Water moves by osmosis from the hypotonic solution into the cell, causing lysis (haemolysis).

questions.q: Active transport requires a supply of ATP because it moves substances:
questions.explain: Pumping solutes from low to high concentration needs energy from ATP (e.g. the sodium–potassium pump).

questions.q: The uptake of large particles or fluid into a cell by the membrane folding inward is called:
questions.explain: In endocytosis the membrane engulfs material into a vesicle; exocytosis releases material out of the cell.

questions.q: Cholesterol in animal cell membranes helps to:
questions.explain: Cholesterol stabilises fluidity across a range of temperatures.

questions.q: A major benefit of compartmentalization by internal membranes is that it:
options: Allows incompatible reactions to occur simultaneously in separate spaces
questions.explain: Membrane-bound organelles keep optimal conditions and separate processes (e.g. digestion in lysosomes).

questions.q: The double membrane and internal cristae are features of the:
questions.explain: Cristae increase the surface area for the electron transport chain in aerobic respiration.

questions.q: Proteins destined for secretion are typically processed in the following sequence:
options: Rough ER → Golgi apparatus → secretory vesicle
questions.explain: Proteins made on the rough ER are modified and packaged by the Golgi, then exported in vesicles.

questions.q: Cells that secrete large amounts of digestive enzymes would be expected to contain especially large numbers of:
questions.explain: High protein synthesis and secretion demands abundant ribosomes, rough ER and Golgi.

questions.q: The site of ribosome subunit assembly within the nucleus is the:
questions.explain: The nucleolus manufactures ribosomal RNA and assembles ribosome subunits.

questions.q: Cell specialization (differentiation) occurs because different cell types:
options: Express different subsets of their genes
questions.explain: Differentiated cells share the same genome but switch on different genes, producing different proteins.

questions.q: A stem cell is best defined as a cell that can:
options: Divide and differentiate into other cell types
questions.explain: Stem cells retain the capacity for self-renewal and differentiation.

questions.q: A cell described as pluripotent can differentiate into:
options: Almost all cell types of the body
A whole new organism including placenta
questions.explain: Pluripotent cells (e.g. embryonic stem cells) form nearly all body cell types; totipotent cells can also form extra-embryonic tissue.

questions.q: The biconcave, enucleate shape of a red blood cell is an adaptation that:
options: Increases surface area and space for oxygen transport
questions.explain: Loss of the nucleus and the biconcave shape maximise haemoglobin content and gas exchange.

questions.q: Which factor would most increase the rate of diffusion across a membrane?
questions.explain: Rate of diffusion rises with a steeper gradient, larger surface area, shorter distance and smaller molecules.

questions.q: Compared with a prokaryote, a eukaryotic cell can achieve higher metabolic efficiency partly because compartmentalization:
options: Concentrates enzymes and substrates in specific organelles
questions.explain: Localising pathways raises reaction efficiency and allows fine control.

questions.q: Muscle cells contain many mitochondria because they:
options: Have a high demand for ATP
questions.explain: Contraction requires large amounts of ATP, met by numerous mitochondria.

questions.q: Osmosis is specifically the movement of:
options: Water across a partially permeable membrane down its water potential gradient
questions.explain: Osmosis refers only to water movement, from higher to lower water potential.
